title: A bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker DOES exempt a quoted value in all five slot guards — the closing quote satisfies the "has a reason" test, contradicting systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169
description:
**BLUF:** the platform rule says a bare `slot-literal-ok:` marker exempts nothing, but on a **quoted value** (JSON, or any line where the marker is not last) the value's own closing quote satisfies the "has a reason" test, so **a bare marker DOES exempt**. Measured in all five harness guards' shared regex shape. Found while fixing KS-1450; not introduced by it.

## The rule it contradicts

`systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169`, verbatim:

> A deliberate exception carries `slot-literal-ok: <reason>` on the same line; a bare marker exempts nothing.

## The defect

Every implementation tests for "marker, optional whitespace, then one non-whitespace character":

```
no_hardcoded_slot_literals.test.sh   grep -vE 'slot-literal-ok:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]'
playwright/.../no-hardcoded-slot-literals.test.ts:79    const MARKER = /slot-literal-ok:\s*\S/
performance/.../noHardcodedSlotLiterals.test.ts:49      const MARKER = 'slot-literal-ok:'
schemathesis/.../test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:50   _OPT_OUT = "slot-literal-ok:"
akto/tests/unit/config/noTypedSlotValues.test.ts        (same shape)
```

`[^[:space:]]` / `\S` is satisfied by **any** non-space character, including `"`. So:

```
  "reason": "x 6982 slot-literal-ok:",      -> EXEMPTED   (wrong: the reason is empty)
const p = 6982; // slot-literal-ok:          -> reported   (right)
```

Driven both ways in one call against the same regex. The only reason this has never shown up is that every existing marker sits in a `#` or `//` comment at true end-of-line, where nothing follows the colon — which is also why the suites' own controls pass: each plants its bare-marker fixture into a comment, never into a quoted value. `test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:263` asserts "the bare marker does not \[exempt\]" and passes for exactly that reason.

## Why it matters now

KS-1450 is the first change to put `slot-literal-ok` markers inside JSON string values (the six `accepted.*.reason` entries of `systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis-baseline.json`). Before it, that file carried **zero** markers, so the gap was latent. It is recorded as a named limitation in KS-1450's PR Test Evidence rather than fixed there, because a one-guard fix would make the five guards disagree about what a bare marker means.

## Suggested fix

Require a reason character that is not structural, e.g. tighten the class to `[^[:space:]",]` (and the JS/Python equivalents) in **all five** implementations in one change, so they stay in agreement.

**Blast radius, measured before proposing it:** exactly **2** existing marker lines repo-wide would lose exemption, and **neither needs it** — `systemTest/schemathesis/tests/unit/test_no_hardcoded_slot_numbers.py:50` (`_OPT_OUT = "slot-literal-ok:"`, a constant; the line holds no slot literal) and the shell guard's own bare-marker control line (its port is computed, not typed). So nothing that passes today would go red.

Each implementation should also gain a control that plants the bare marker into a **quoted value**, not only into a comment — the absence of that control is what hid this.

## Provenance

* Both-way measurement and the blast-radius count: Seat R 16th, 2026-10-08, during KS-1450.
* The rule: `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1169`.
* The guard: KS-1386 (Done, Peter).
